findings.rationale: CO's uploaded updates are roughly 3-4x the median norm in nearly every round (size-adjusted z=+7.6), starting in round 1, and their cosine to the median update is weak (mean 0.13) and changes sign from round to round. That pattern fits large random noise added to uploads rather than a consistent sign-flip or scaling. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.83, CITL 0.018), so this is not a label or prevalence fault. Confidence is moderate because the fault type is inferred from the update pattern alone.

MA's update norms are about 2-4x the median in every round (size-adjusted z=+6.8), starting in round 1. Mean cosine to the median update is weak (0.20) and ranges from -0.37 to 0.98 across rounds, which looks like random noise rather than a coherent manipulation. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.86, CITL 0.008).

WA's update norms are 3-8x the median (size-adjusted z=+7.0), starting in round 1 and shrinking slowly over the rounds. Mean cosine to the median update is 0.29, with a wide spread and no consistent sign, which fits added noise. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.82, CITL 0.010). Confidence is lower than for CO and MA because WA is the largest client, so part of its norm excess could be size-related, although the tool already adjusts for size.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of the update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then confirmed suspicions per client. Three clients (CO, MA, WA) show consistently inflated update norms from round 1 (size-adjusted z of about +7) with near-zero, unstable cosine to the median update, while their local AUC and calibration stay normal. I classed them as explanation_instability (random-noise uploads), with moderate confidence on the fault type and lower confidence for WA. I did not report GU, AK, MD, SC, MT, DC or the drift and feature outliers: their signals were small, from small clients, inconsistent across calls, or failed to reproduce, so they look like noise. Label-noise, prevalence-shift, drift, missing-artefact, subgroup-bias and free-rider screens showed no consistent client-level signal. The federation-wide attribution churn is high in early rounds but cannot be attributed to a single client. The full budget of 20 epsilon is spent.
